title: Lemongrass Tofu with Steamed Jasmine Rice
ingredients: 300 g firm tofu; 2 stalks lemongrass, finely minced; 1 shallot; 1 tbsp soy sauce; 1 tsp brown sugar; 1 tbsp neutral oil; cooked jasmine rice
steps: Press the tofu for 15 minutes and cut it into bite-sized cubes. Keep the minced lemongrass separate from any tough outer leaves.
Pan-fry the tofu in the oil until golden on two sides, then transfer it to a plate.
Soften the shallot and lemongrass over medium heat. Add the soy sauce, sugar and two tablespoons of water, then return the tofu and toss gently.
Serve over warm rice with sliced cucumber and fresh coriander. Taste before adding extra soy sauce.

title: Ginger Mushroom Clay-Pot Style Stew
ingredients: 350 g mixed mushrooms; 200 g firm tofu; 15 g ginger; 2 tbsp soy sauce; 1 tsp sugar; 150 ml water; black pepper; sliced spring onion
steps: Wipe the mushrooms clean and tear larger pieces into similar sizes. Cut the tofu into thick slices.
Brown the mushrooms in a heavy saucepan in two batches so that they do not steam.
Add the ginger, tofu, soy sauce, sugar and water. Cover and simmer gently for 12 minutes.
Uncover briefly to reduce the sauce. Finish with black pepper and spring onion, then serve with rice.

title: Roasted Pumpkin and Coconut Soup
ingredients: 600 g peeled pumpkin; 1 onion; 200 ml coconut milk; 500 ml vegetable stock; 1 tbsp olive oil; ground cumin; salt; pumpkin seeds
steps: Cut the pumpkin into small wedges, coat with half the oil and roast at 200 C until tender and lightly browned.
Soften the chopped onion in a saucepan with the remaining oil and a pinch of cumin.
Add the pumpkin and vegetable stock. Simmer for 10 minutes, then blend until smooth.
Stir in the coconut milk and warm through without boiling hard. Season to taste and scatter pumpkin seeds on top.

title: Vietnamese Tomato and Tofu Noodle Soup
ingredients: 250 g rice noodles; 250 g firm tofu; 4 ripe tomatoes; 1 litre vegetable stock; 1 shallot; 1 tbsp soy sauce; 1 tbsp oil; fresh herbs
steps: Cook the rice noodles according to their package instructions, rinse briefly and divide between bowls.
Pan-fry cubes of tofu until the edges are golden. Set aside while softening the shallot in the same pan.
Add chopped tomatoes and cook until they release their juices. Pour in the vegetable stock and soy sauce, then simmer for 12 minutes.
Add the tofu to the broth for the final few minutes. Ladle over the noodles and finish with fresh herbs.

title: Garlic Morning Glory with Sesame
ingredients: 400 g morning glory; 4 garlic cloves; 1 tbsp neutral oil; 1 tbsp soy sauce; 1 tsp toasted sesame seeds; 2 tbsp water
steps: Wash the morning glory thoroughly and separate thick stems from the tender leaves.
Heat a wide pan and briefly soften the sliced garlic in oil without letting it burn.
Add the stems first with the water, then add the leaves and soy sauce. Toss until just wilted.
Transfer to a serving plate immediately and sprinkle with sesame seeds. Serve while the stems are still crisp.

title: Braised Eggplant with Tofu and Basil
ingredients: 2 medium eggplants; 250 g tofu; 2 garlic cloves; 1 tbsp soy sauce; 1 tbsp tomato paste; 200 ml vegetable stock; 1 tbsp oil; basil
steps: Cut the eggplants into thick pieces and pat the tofu dry before cubing it.
Brown the eggplant in a wide pan with the oil, working in batches if needed.
Add garlic and tomato paste, followed by the stock, soy sauce and tofu. Cover and simmer until the eggplant is soft.
Remove the lid to thicken the sauce slightly. Tear in the basil just before serving with rice.

title: Crisp Tofu and Cabbage Rice Bowl
ingredients: 300 g firm tofu; 200 g shredded cabbage; 1 carrot; cooked brown rice; 1 tbsp soy sauce; juice of half a lime; 1 tsp sugar; 1 tbsp oil
steps: Press and cube the tofu. Shred the cabbage and carrot finely, keeping them separate from the raw tofu preparation area.
Pan-fry the tofu in oil until crisp around the edges. Toss with half the soy sauce.
Mix the remaining soy sauce with lime juice, sugar and a little water to make a dressing.
Build bowls with rice, tofu and crunchy vegetables. Spoon over the dressing just before eating.

title: Sweet Potato and Red Lentil Curry
ingredients: 2 medium sweet potatoes; 150 g red lentils; 1 onion; 400 ml coconut milk; 400 ml vegetable stock; 1 tbsp curry powder; 1 tbsp oil; lime
steps: Rinse the lentils until the water runs mostly clear and cut the peeled sweet potatoes into small cubes.
Soften the onion in oil, then stir in the curry powder for 30 seconds.
Add the lentils, sweet potatoes, coconut milk and stock. Simmer gently for 20 minutes, stirring occasionally and adding water if needed.
Check that the sweet potatoes are tender and the lentils have softened. Finish with lime juice and serve with rice.

title: Caramelized Tofu with Black Pepper
ingredients: 300 g firm tofu; 1 tbsp brown sugar; 1 tbsp soy sauce; 100 ml water; 1 shallot; 1 tsp cracked black pepper; 1 tbsp oil
steps: Pat the tofu dry, cut it into thick rectangles and pan-fry until golden.
Soften the sliced shallot in a small saucepan. Add the sugar with one tablespoon of water and let it dissolve gently.
Stir in the remaining water, soy sauce and pepper. Add the tofu and simmer for 8 minutes, turning the pieces carefully.
Reduce the sauce until it lightly coats the tofu. Serve with plain rice and steamed greens.

title: Oyster Mushroom and Bok Choy Stir-Fry
ingredients: 300 g oyster mushrooms; 3 small bok choy; 2 garlic cloves; 1 tbsp soy sauce; 1 tsp cornstarch; 80 ml water; 1 tbsp oil
steps: Tear the mushrooms into strips and separate the bok choy leaves, washing away any soil near the stems.
Sear the mushrooms in a hot pan with oil until their edges start to brown.
Add the garlic and bok choy stems, followed by the leaves. Stir the cornstarch into the water and soy sauce, then pour into the pan.
Toss until the sauce thickens and the greens are tender but not soft. Serve immediately.

title: Vegetable and Mushroom Hot Pot
ingredients: 1.5 litres vegetable stock; 300 g mixed mushrooms; 250 g tofu; 1 small Chinese cabbage; 1 carrot; 200 g rice noodles; ginger; soy sauce
steps: Warm the stock with sliced ginger and a small splash of soy sauce. Taste the broth before adding vegetables.
Arrange cleaned mushrooms, tofu, sliced carrot and cabbage on separate plates for easy cooking.
Add the carrot and firm mushroom pieces first, then the tofu and leafy vegetables. Simmer until cooked through.
Cook the rice noodles separately and add them to individual bowls before spooning over the broth and vegetables.

title: Tangy Pineapple and Tomato Vegetable Broth
ingredients: 250 g pineapple; 3 tomatoes; 150 g okra; 200 g tofu; 1 litre vegetable stock; 1 tbsp tamarind paste; 1 tbsp soy sauce; fresh herbs
steps: Slice the pineapple and tomatoes, trim the okra and cut the tofu into cubes.
Bring the vegetable stock to a gentle simmer and stir in tamarind paste and soy sauce.
Add pineapple and tomatoes first, then okra and tofu. Simmer just until the okra is tender.
Taste for a balance of sourness and sweetness. Finish with fresh herbs and serve alongside rice.

title: Creamy White Bean and Spinach Skillet
ingredients: 2 cans white beans, drained; 150 g spinach; 1 onion; 2 garlic cloves; 200 ml vegetable stock; 100 ml unsweetened oat cream; 1 tbsp olive oil; lemon
steps: Soften the onion in olive oil and add the garlic for the final minute.
Add the drained beans and vegetable stock, then simmer for 5 minutes.
Mash a few beans into the liquid before stirring in oat cream and spinach.
Cook until the spinach wilts. Add lemon juice to taste and serve with toasted bread.

title: Lemon Chickpea Couscous Salad
ingredients: 150 g couscous; 1 can chickpeas, drained; 1 cucumber; 1 red pepper; parsley; 2 tbsp olive oil; juice of 1 lemon; salt
steps: Prepare the couscous with the amount of hot water stated on its packet, then fluff with a fork and let it cool.
Dice the cucumber and pepper into small pieces and roughly chop the parsley.
Whisk the olive oil and lemon juice together. Fold the dressing through the couscous with chickpeas and vegetables.
Season to taste and let the salad stand for 10 minutes before serving so the flavours can settle.

title: Roasted Cauliflower Tacos with Lime Slaw
ingredients: 1 cauliflower; 8 corn tortillas; 150 g red cabbage; 1 lime; 1 tsp smoked paprika; 2 tbsp olive oil; 3 tbsp unsweetened soy yogurt; coriander
steps: Cut the cauliflower into small florets, toss with paprika and half the oil, and roast at 210 C until browned.
Finely shred the cabbage and dress it with lime juice and the remaining oil.
Warm the tortillas in a dry pan and loosen the soy yogurt with a little water and lime juice.
Fill each tortilla with cauliflower and slaw. Add the yogurt dressing and coriander just before serving.

title: Mushroom and Pea Barley Risotto
ingredients: 180 g pearl barley; 250 g mushrooms; 100 g frozen peas; 1 onion; 900 ml warm vegetable stock; 2 tbsp olive oil; parsley; black pepper
steps: Rinse the barley. In a wide saucepan, soften the onion in half the olive oil.
Add barley and a ladle of warm stock. Continue adding stock gradually while the barley simmers, stirring regularly.
Brown the mushrooms in a separate pan with the remaining oil. Fold them into the barley with the peas near the end of cooking.
When the barley is tender with a slight bite, add parsley and black pepper. Rest for a few minutes before serving.

title: Tomato Basil Pasta with Butter Beans
ingredients: 200 g pasta without egg; 1 can butter beans, drained; 400 g chopped tomatoes; 2 garlic cloves; 1 tbsp olive oil; basil; salt; black pepper
steps: Cook the pasta in salted water until just tender, reserving a cup of the cooking water.
Warm the garlic in olive oil, add the tomatoes and simmer for 15 minutes.
Fold the butter beans into the sauce and warm through. Add the pasta with a little reserved water to loosen the sauce.
Tear in the basil and season with black pepper. Serve immediately while the sauce coats the pasta.

title: Peanut-Free Sesame Noodles with Crunchy Vegetables
ingredients: 200 g wheat noodles without egg; 1 carrot; 1 cucumber; 150 g edamame; 2 tbsp tahini; 1 tbsp soy sauce; 1 tbsp rice vinegar; warm water
steps: Cook the noodles and edamame according to their packet instructions, then drain and cool briefly.
Slice the carrot and cucumber into fine strips.
Whisk tahini, soy sauce, rice vinegar and enough warm water to make a pourable dressing.
Toss the noodles with vegetables and dressing. This recipe contains sesame, soy and wheat; check individual ingredient labels for your needs.

title: Warm Lentil and Roasted Carrot Salad
ingredients: 160 g green lentils; 4 carrots; 1 small red onion; parsley; 2 tbsp olive oil; 1 tbsp red wine vinegar; 1 tsp mustard; salt
steps: Cook the lentils in water until tender, then drain well. Check the packet for the cooking time of your variety.
Cut the carrots into batons and roast with half the olive oil at 200 C until their edges brown.
Whisk the remaining oil with vinegar and mustard. Finely slice the red onion and chop the parsley.
Combine the warm lentils, carrots, onion and dressing. Finish with parsley and season to taste.

title: Vietnamese Fresh Rolls with Tofu and Herbs
ingredients: 8 rice paper sheets; 200 g firm tofu; 100 g rice vermicelli; lettuce; mint; cucumber; 2 tbsp soy sauce; lime juice; water
steps: Cook and cool the vermicelli. Pan-fry tofu strips and let them cool before assembling the rolls.
Wash the herbs and lettuce, pat them dry and slice the cucumber into thin batons.
Soften one rice paper sheet at a time in water. Add a small amount of each filling and fold the sides in before rolling firmly.
Mix soy sauce with lime juice and a little water for dipping. Keep finished rolls separated so they do not stick together.

title: Coconut Banana Oat Muffins
ingredients: 2 ripe bananas; 180 g plain flour; 60 g rolled oats; 120 ml coconut milk; 50 ml neutral oil; 60 g sugar; 2 tsp baking powder; pinch of salt
steps: Heat the oven to 180 C and line a muffin tin. Mash the bananas in a large bowl.
Mix coconut milk, oil and sugar into the banana. Stir flour, oats, baking powder and salt together separately.
Fold the dry mixture into the wet mixture just until combined. Divide the batter between muffin cases.
Bake for about 20 to 25 minutes, checking that a skewer inserted into the centre comes out clean. Cool on a rack.

title: Apple Cinnamon Crumble with Oat Topping
ingredients: 4 apples; 80 g rolled oats; 70 g plain flour; 60 g plant-based baking spread; 50 g brown sugar; 1 tsp cinnamon; 2 tbsp water
steps: Heat the oven to 180 C. Slice the apples and place them in a baking dish with cinnamon and water.
Rub the flour and plant-based spread together until the mixture resembles coarse crumbs.
Mix the oats and sugar into the crumbs and scatter the topping loosely over the apples.
Bake until the topping is golden and the fruit is soft, about 30 to 35 minutes. Let it cool briefly before serving.

title: Orange and Olive Oil Tea Loaf
ingredients: 220 g plain flour; 110 g sugar; 180 ml orange juice; zest of 1 orange; 70 ml mild olive oil; 2 tsp baking powder; pinch of salt
steps: Heat the oven to 175 C and line a small loaf tin with baking paper.
Combine orange juice, zest, sugar and olive oil in a bowl.
Sift in flour, baking powder and salt, then fold gently until no dry patches remain.
Pour into the tin and bake until a skewer comes out clean, checking from 35 minutes onward. Cool fully before slicing.

title: Spinach and Feta Omelette with Cherry Tomatoes
ingredients: 3 eggs; 80 g spinach; 40 g feta made with vegetarian rennet; 8 cherry tomatoes; 1 tsp olive oil; black pepper
steps: Check that the feta is suitable for vegetarians, then crumble it into small pieces. Halve the tomatoes.
Wilt the spinach in a non-stick pan with olive oil and briefly soften the tomatoes.
Beat the eggs, pour them into the pan and cook gently until mostly set. Scatter over the feta.
Fold the omelette and cook until the egg is fully set. Serve promptly with black pepper. This is an egg-and-dairy vegetarian dish, not vegan.

title: Mushroom and Cheese Toast with Garden Herbs
ingredients: 250 g mushrooms; 4 bread slices; 60 g vegetarian cheddar; 1 tbsp olive oil; 1 garlic clove; parsley; black pepper
steps: Slice the mushrooms and check that the cheese uses vegetarian rennet.
Cook the mushrooms in olive oil until their moisture has evaporated, then add chopped garlic.
Toast the bread lightly, divide the mushrooms over it and top with grated cheese.
Grill until the cheese melts and finish with parsley and pepper. This recipe contains dairy and wheat.

title: Crispy Rice Pancakes with Mushroom Filling
ingredients: 150 g rice flour; 50 g cornstarch; 250 ml water; 100 ml coconut milk; 1 tsp turmeric; 200 g mushrooms; 100 g bean sprouts; oil; lettuce
steps: Whisk rice flour, cornstarch, turmeric, water and coconut milk into a thin batter. Rest while preparing the filling.
Slice and stir-fry the mushrooms until cooked. Rinse the bean sprouts and drain thoroughly.
Heat a lightly oiled non-stick pan, add a thin layer of batter and scatter mushrooms and sprouts over one half.
Cover briefly to cook the filling, then uncover to crisp the edges. Fold and serve with lettuce and a plant-based dipping sauce.

title: Braised Cabbage and Mushrooms in Ginger Broth
ingredients: 1 small cabbage; 250 g mushrooms; 15 g ginger; 250 ml vegetable stock; 1 tbsp soy sauce; 1 tbsp oil; spring onion
steps: Cut the cabbage into wedges that hold together at the stem and slice the mushrooms.
Brown the cabbage wedges lightly in oil, turning them carefully with a spatula.
Add mushrooms, sliced ginger, stock and soy sauce. Cover and simmer until the cabbage is tender.
Spoon the broth over the wedges, finish with spring onion and serve with steamed rice.

title: Coconut Mushroom Hot Pot with Rice Noodles
ingredients: 800 ml vegetable stock; 300 ml coconut milk; 350 g mushrooms; 200 g tofu; 200 g rice noodles; 1 lemongrass stalk; lime; leafy greens
steps: Bruise the lemongrass stalk and simmer it in vegetable stock for 10 minutes, then remove it.
Add coconut milk and bring the broth back to a gentle simmer without boiling vigorously.
Add mushrooms, tofu and greens in stages so that everything cooks evenly. Cook the noodles separately.
Serve the vegetables and broth over noodles. Add lime juice to each bowl to keep the citrus flavour bright.

title: Green Pea and Mint Soup with Toasted Seeds
ingredients: 400 g frozen peas; 1 onion; 650 ml vegetable stock; a small handful of mint; 1 tbsp olive oil; sunflower seeds; lemon juice
steps: Soften the onion slowly in olive oil until translucent rather than browned.
Add stock and bring to a simmer. Add the peas and cook just until tender.
Stir in the mint and blend until smooth, adding a little water if a thinner texture is preferred.
Taste with a small squeeze of lemon and serve topped with toasted sunflower seeds.

title: Tofu Fried Rice with Carrot and Green Beans
ingredients: 450 g cooked rice, properly chilled; 200 g firm tofu; 1 carrot; 150 g green beans; 2 spring onions; 1 tbsp soy sauce; 1 tbsp oil
steps: Dice the carrot and beans finely. Crumble the tofu into small pieces and separate clumps of chilled rice with a fork.
Stir-fry the carrot and beans in oil until nearly tender, then add the tofu.
Add the rice and soy sauce and stir-fry until the rice is steaming hot throughout.
Fold in spring onion and serve immediately. Use rice that was cooled promptly and stored in the refrigerator, and reheat it only once.

title: Building a Practical Plant-Based Pantry
content: A useful pantry starts with ingredients you actually enjoy cooking. Keep a small selection of beans, lentils, rice, pasta, canned tomatoes and seasonings that work across several dishes. Add one versatile nut or seed butter if it suits your household. Before shopping, choose two meals that share ingredients and check what is already open in the cupboard. Label opened packets and rotate older items to the front. A compact, well-used pantry is often more practical than a shelf full of unfamiliar products.

title: A Sunday Prep Session for Three Weeknight Dinners
content: Start with a pot of rice, a tray of roasted vegetables and a batch of pan-fried tofu. While these cook, wash herbs and prepare a simple lime-and-soy dressing. Keep each component in its own container so dinner can take different forms: a rice bowl, fresh rolls or a warm vegetable skillet. Cool cooked food promptly and refrigerate it in shallow containers. Follow local food-storage guidance and the instructions for each ingredient. Prep components rather than identical finished meals to keep the week interesting.

title: How to Make Mushrooms Brown Instead of Steam
content: Mushrooms need room in the pan if you want browned edges. Wipe away dirt, cut them into similar pieces and start with a hot, wide pan. Cook in batches instead of piling everything in at once. Let the first side sit against the pan before stirring, then add softer aromatics such as garlic near the end so they do not burn. Finish with a little soy sauce after the mushrooms have browned. The same batch can become a noodle topping, toast filling or side dish for rice.

title: Keeping Fresh Herbs Useful Throughout the Week
content: Sort herbs when you bring them home and remove damaged leaves. Wash only what you plan to use immediately, or dry washed herbs thoroughly before storing them. Wrap tender herbs loosely in a clean, slightly damp towel inside a container and check them regularly. Chop small leftover amounts into a dressing or scatter them over soup just before serving. Keep mint, coriander and basil separate when their flavours would overwhelm one another. Good storage helps, but planning a second dish for the same bunch is the simplest way to reduce waste.

title: Choosing a Plant-Based Dipping Sauce for Fresh Rolls
content: Fresh rolls work well with a dipping sauce that balances savoury, sour and sweet flavours. Begin with soy sauce, lime juice and a little sugar, then dilute with water until the sauce complements the filling rather than dominating it. Add chopped chilli only if everyone at the table wants heat. For a creamy version, use a suitable seed butter and warm water. Check ingredient labels: some bottled dipping sauces contain fish, shrimp or other animal ingredients, and seed-based sauces can still contain allergens.

title: Making Soup More Interesting with Texture
content: A smooth soup can benefit from a contrasting topping. Try a small spoonful of pan-fried mushrooms, crisp chickpeas or toasted seeds, choosing options that fit your household's dietary needs. Keep crunchy toppings separate until serving so they do not soften in the pot. Fresh herbs and a small squeeze of citrus can brighten flavour without changing the whole recipe. When serving several people, put toppings in individual bowls and let everyone finish their own portion. Label toppings clearly if they contain common allergens.

title: Reading Labels for Egg-and-Dairy Vegetarian Cooking
content: Egg-and-dairy vegetarian cooking includes eggs and milk products, but labels still deserve attention. Check cheese for vegetarian rennet and look for gelatine in prepared desserts. A product described as dairy-free may contain egg, while a vegetarian label does not necessarily mean vegan. Keep the distinction clear when sharing a recipe with friends: list the actual ingredients and identify suitable substitutions separately. For guests with allergies, ask about their requirements rather than assuming a vegetarian alternative will be suitable.

title: A Flexible Formula for Seasonal Rice Bowls
content: Choose a cooked grain, a bean or tofu component, two vegetables with different textures and a dressing you enjoy. The formula is flexible: roasted pumpkin and steamed greens can replace cucumber and carrot when the weather changes. Start with small amounts of dressing and add more at the table. Keep garnishes separate for people who prefer a simpler bowl. When adapting a recipe, check the ingredients in sauces as carefully as the main components. Variety comes from changing flavour and texture, not only from buying more ingredients.

title: Making a Vegetable Stock from Everyday Ingredients
content: Use clean onion, carrot, celery or mushroom trimmings to make a simple stock. Avoid spoiled scraps and strongly bitter vegetables that can dominate the flavour. Cover the ingredients with water, simmer gently and strain when the stock tastes balanced. Cool it promptly and store it according to appropriate food-safety guidance. Leave the stock lightly seasoned so it can work in different recipes. Label the container with its contents and preparation date, especially when cooking for people who need to avoid specific ingredients.

title: Preparing a Welcoming Vegetarian Hot Pot Table
content: Arrange firm vegetables, leafy greens, mushrooms, tofu and noodles on separate plates so guests can see what they are choosing. Cook dense ingredients first and delicate leaves near the end. Keep the broth gently simmering and use clean utensils for serving. Offer sauces in small bowls with ingredient labels rather than mixing everything into the main pot. Check that the stock and condiments are plant-based. A shared meal feels more relaxed when everyone understands the cooking order and can choose flavours that suit them.

title: Simple Ways to Use Leftover Roast Vegetables
content: Roasted carrots, cauliflower or pumpkin can become the starting point for another meal when they have been cooled and stored safely. Add them to a bean salad, warm them in a tomato sauce or tuck them into a wrap with greens. Keep the second meal distinct by changing the dressing and texture. Do not repeatedly cool and reheat the same batch. Check food-storage guidance and discard leftovers if you are unsure how they were handled. Planning the second use before cooking the first tray helps prevent forgotten containers.

title: Sharing Clear Recipes with a Plant-Based Community
content: A helpful recipe includes ingredient amounts, serving size, cooking order and a few signs that show when each stage is ready. Mention substitutions you have actually tried and describe how they change the result. If a dish contains eggs or dairy, label it as egg-and-dairy vegetarian rather than vegan. Credit sources that inspired your version and use your own words and photos when possible. Clear details help other cooks ask useful questions and make the community more welcoming to beginners.
